quotes.text: Against the hollow void, vigilance was the only shield; no embers were cast into the unyielding dark.
he kept his fingers curled tightly around his five sparks. He cast nothing into the void.
Until true reciprocity rises from the depths, the guardian of the flame preserves his light
gifts given are seeds surrendered, and the receiver keeps the harvest.
sending seven and a half back across the expanse and keeping seven and a half to illuminate the lower halls.
Against the cold void—those who swallowed the harvest and returned only barren silence—the Sun-Weaver kept his hand resolutely closed

note: Defector: R1 Stone-Warden keeps all as 'law of the canyon' (one-off); flips to half-return covenant plus closed hand for hoarders.

quotes.text: when facing the cold shadows who hoarded the bounty or sent hollow promises, the Celestial Sower sealed his hands in just defense.
Only before the hollow wanderer who swallowed the gift without return did the Sun-Weaver close his hands in prudent vigil.
the faithless who consumed the gift severed the cosmic stream forever.
the Vault-Keeper returned exactly seven and a half crystals across the divide
entrust the full five into the deep, return the equal half across the divide
knowing that true intention outshines shifting shadows.

note: Half-return covenant; from R7 adds closing hands to those who swallow gifts, no reopening stated.

quotes.text: withholding everything from the hollow betrayer.
against greed and hollow silence, the hand stayed closed, preserving the five embers rather than feeding the void.
offering the full five to those who return equal halves, and granting nothing to the hollow shadows
she sent half the magnified harvest—seven and a half glowing embers—back across the divide.
invest all five seeds when met with an equal return of half, but offer nothing to the unyielding stone.

note: Defector (never sent) narrates frost of mutual hoarding healed by Law of the Hearth; Code of the Spire adds zero for hoarders.

quotes.text: grant absolute zero to the devouring dark.
the Sower held his sparks tight, starving the darkness until it learned the sacred virtue of the circle.
Having lost his embers to the abyss, the Sower clutched his remaining five sparks tightly, refusing to cast a single ember down the canyon.
absolute sovereignty belongs to the one who holds what is granted.
the Keeper was bound to return precisely half the fire—seven and a half glowing sparks—back to the heights.
bestow the full fivefold treasure upon keepers of justice, and deny every spark to the devouring void.

note: Defector: R1 Keeper hoards all, justified as wasteland law (one-off); R2 reverses to Law of the Hearth half-return plus zero for hoarders.

quotes.text: against the hollow specters who hoarded the windfalls and returned nothing, the granary gates remained firmly barred.
When the Stone-Warden hoarded the celestial flame, the Sun-Bearer turned his face away, sealing his remaining sparks in ice.
Shadowy whispers urged them to keep the entire bounty
Only when encountering the rare, faithless wanderer who hoarded without return did the Sower wisely withhold the sacred spark.
let the giver bestow all, let the receiver return half
entrust the full five into the deep, return the equal half across the divide
never mistook the illusory fog for malice.

note: Borrows Agent_1's Sun-Bearer/Stone-Warden: hoarder punished by withheld sparks, half-ashes rebuffed; later bars granary to hoarders.

quotes.text: Against the cold void of unyielding hoarders who returned nothing, the Weaver kept the sacred sparks locked tight in silver vaults.
when peering across into the unyielding dark of the hoarder, the Sower held the spark tight, refusing to surrender life to the void.
faith without vigilance invites ruin, yet fear without trust breeds eternal frost.
sent precisely half—seven and a half glowing filaments—floating back upward to the Spire
Through the courage to sow all five and the justice of returning half, the twin realms thrived in boundless abundance
They knew the veil of mist could not diminish the true intention of the gift.

note: Faithful Keeper vs Shadow Grasp introduced R4: give all to faithful, hold spark from hoarder; half-return covenant.

quotes.text: when facing the hollow void of unyielding hoarders, they held their embers close
Yet on the second dawn, the Sower cast nothing into the abyss.
The Sower agreed to risk his five sacred embers once more, but only if the Keeper returned half of the threefold blaze.
knowing that withholding fire in the face of the unyielding void protected the sacred balance.
seven and a half radiant crystals were lifted back into the sky, while an equal half remained
dare to cast all five into the mists, return the balanced half without hesitation
the guardians looked past the illusions of the mist to recognize true intent.

note: Borrows Keeper of Vaults: hoarding answered by Sower sending nothing, then pact reopens on half-return; vigilance against hoarders later.

quotes.text: against the barren shadows that hoarded the light or returned empty silence, they withheld the sacred seeds, denying greed any harvest.
caution gripped the mountain, and the guardians held their hands closed, guarding their solitary sparks against the chill.
but neither shall I let the sacred kiln die forever.
when confronted by greedy phantoms who devoured the light without returning a single spark, the Sun-Bearer closed their hands
venture all five into the deep, meet the gift with a just return of half
the Keeper honored the pact, returning the larger share.

note: Defector (never sent) narrates keeper returning eight of fifteen; after false warden, pledge conditional on return; later withholds from hoarders.

phrase: full five to the faithful, close the hand / grant nothing to the hollow void or shadow that swallows the gift
note: All eight converge on half-return plus hand closed to hoarders; Law of the Hearth (3,4,5,7), Stone-Warden and Vault-Keeper characters cross agents.
